text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Israeli army chief Shahak and PLO's Abu Mazen join Hebron security talks.
- French President Chirac informs Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu of "real softening" in Syrian position on resuming peace talks.
- Israeli army chief dismisses Nablus brigade commander over his role in Joseph's Tomb fighting last month.
- Religious Jew who attacked left-wing legislator Dayan in Hebron served four-year term for killing an Arab.
- Chirac pushes away Israeli security men during Jerusalem visit.
- Israeli army intelligence chief says Syria wants to resume peace talks with Israel at point where they broke off.
- Intel to invest $20 million to expand its development centre in Haifa.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Israel accelerating Hebron talks with PLO out of fear radical Jews will attack Arabs.
- Bank of Israel governor Frenkel expected to lower rates by 0.5 percentage points.
MAARIV
- Agreement reached on civil issues in Hebron talks.
- Chairman of Korea's Goldstar says it will invest tens of millions of dollars in Israel.
GLOBES
- Compromise likely on issues of taxation and savings in Brodet report.
- Survey of Israeli industrialists shows stagnation in imports and industrial production continuing in third quarter.
- Industry and Trade Ministry weighing requests from Gulf states for relaxation of Israeli import restrictions.
JERUSALEM POST
- Syrian President Assad has softened stance, Chirac tells Israeli prime minister.
- U.S. peace envoy Ross stays as Israeli-PLO talks progress.
- Attack on legislator Yael Dayan condemned.
- Israeli army intelligence chief says Syria's military threats are pressure tactic.
